IS : 5083 - 1988

Indian Standard SPECIFICATION FOR KNIFING STOPPER (Second Revision)
0. FOREWORD
0.3 This standard was first published in 1969 In the first revision, the requirements for dents in the determination of stopping properties had been improved and drying schedule of the material modified. The requirement for wateT content had also been modified Jn the second revision, the drying time requirements have been suitably modified to remove ambiguity Consistency clause has also been modified to specify the width of knife and determination of stopping properties, and a method of test for assessing the adhesion of the material to the primer and to the subsequent coats and within the different coats of the material has been added 0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2-1960* The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard *Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised ). 3.3 Consistency -- The material shall be suitable for application by a knife of about 30 cm width and produce a smooth and uniform surface. It should be capable of being drawn smoothly with knife for about 125 cm length at a stretch for airdrying synthetic system 3.4 The material shall be compatible with petroleum hydrocarbon solvent 145/205 ( low aromatic ) ( see IS 1745-1978*) 3.5 Stopping Properties -- The material shall pass the test as prescribed in Appendix A 3.6 Rubbing Properties -- The material shall pass the test as prescribed in Appendix B. 3.7 Hold-Out Properties -- The material shall pass the test as prescribed in Appendix C. 3.8 Adhesion and Compatibility in Paint System -- The material shall have good adhesion
( second revision ).

0.1 This Indian Standard ( Second Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 30 March 1988, after the draft finalized by the Paints and Allied Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council 0.2 As part of the painting schedule for finishing rail coaches, manufacturers indent paste filler for colour coats ( see IS 110-1983*) With the advent of welded integral coaches, the use of a knifing stopper was keenly felt in the painting schedule for filling up dents and uneven spots and surface imperfections, and this standard was drawn up in consultation with rail coach manufacturers and embodies the accumulated experience in the supply of the material by manufacturers and users As the performance of the material is dependent on the painting system and schedule of which it forms a part, for proper evaluation of the material, the test schedule should simulate the one to be followed in actual use ( see also Appendix D ). *Specification for ready mixed paint, brushing, grey filler, for enamels, for use over primers ( second revision ) 1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes requirements, and methods of sampling and test for knifing stopper. This material is used for filling up dents and uneven spots, in conjunction with other materials This material constitutes a part of the painting schedule for rail coaches. 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.1 For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given in IS : 1303-1983* shall apply. 3. REQUIREMENTS 3.1 F o r m and Condition -- The material shall be homogeneous soft paste and shall be free from grit and other visible impurities. 3.2 Composition -- The material shall be of such composition as to comply with the requirements of this standard. *Glossary of terms relating to paints ( second revision ). 1

*Specification for petroleum

hydrocarbon solvent

The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the standard mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

5. SAMPLING 5.1 Representative samples of the material shall be drawn as prescribed in IS : 101 ( Part 1/Sec 1 )1986*. 6. TEST METHODS 6.1 Tests shall be conducted as prescribed in IS : 10l-1964 and Appendices A to D. References to IS : 101-1964 are given is col 4 of Table 1 and to appendices in 3.5 to 3.8. 6.2 Quality of Reagents -- Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and distilled water ( see IS : 1070-1977 ) shall be employed in tests.
NOTE -- Pure chemicals shall mean chemicals that do not contain impurities which affect the results of analysis. *Methods of sampling and test for paints, varnishes and related products : Part 1 Test on liquid paints ( general and physical ), Section 1 Sampling. APPENDIX A
( Clause 3.5 )
DETERMINATION OF STOPPING PROPERTIES A-0. GENERAL A-0.1 Outline of the Method -- A mild steel panel is dented with a specified number of dents and then coated with primer and knifing stopper. It is then suitably examined at the dents for satisfactory stopping properties. A-1. PROCEDURE A-1.1 Dent a 300�150�0.900 mm mild steel panel with blunt iron ball hammer with 10 dents 2 of about 3 mm diameter and 1 mm deep. The dents shall be so made that they are 50 mm away from the sides of the panel and 50 mm apart from one another. Roughen the panel with emery paper No. 180. Wipe this with petroleum hydrocarbon solvent, 145/205 ( low aromatic ) ( see IS : 1745-1978* ) and allow to dry. Apply
*Specification for ( second revision ). petroleum hydrocarbon solvents

IS : 5083 - 1988 a coat of red oxide-zinc chromate primer ( see IS : 2074-1979* ) and allow to air-dry for 18 hours. Over this, make one application of the
*Specification for ready mixed paints, red oxide-zinc chrome, priming (first revision ).

material to a thickness of 1 000 microns (wet film thickness ). Keep the panel vertical. A-l.1.1 The material shall be deemed to have passed the test if there is no sagging, shows no signs of crack and pinholes or appreciable shrinkage when observed 18 hours after application.

APPENDIX B ( Clause 36 )
DETERMINATION OF RUBBING PROPERTIES B-0. GENERAL B-0.1 Outline of the Method -- The material in a specified film thickness is applied on a surface prepared by coating with red oxide-zinc chromate primer. This film is then tested for its rubbing properties by rubbing with wet abrasive paper. B-1. PROCEDURE B-1.1 Brush on a mild steel panel, one coat of red oxide-zinc chromate primer ( see IS : 20741979* ) and allow to dry for 18 hours under laboratory drying conditions. Using putty knife,
*Specification for ready mixed paints, red oxide-zinc chrome, priming (first revision ).

apply one coat of the material to give a dry film thickness of not less then 0.30 mm. Allow this to dry for 12 hours under normal laboratory drying conditions. B-1.2 The film prepared as above shall be suitable for wet rubbing down with No. 220 waterproof abrasive paper without any clogging of the paper. Eight rubs under moderate pressure should not remove the material to an extent as to expose the under surface. After rubbing down, the surface shall not show defects like roughness, scratches, cracks, pinholes, etc. These characteristics shall be compared with the registered sample which shall be submitted before bulk supply. Minor pinholes or scratches which will duly be filled by the subsequent coat of filler, shall not be the cause for rejection.

APPENDIX C ( Clause 3.7 )
DETERMINATION OF HOLD-OUT PROPERTIES C-0. GENERAL C-0.1 Outline of the Method -- The film prepared, as for test under Appendix A, is wet rubbed with abrasive paper and a coat of grey ready mixed filler brushed on it. The coat of the ready mixed filler is wet rubbed and a coat of finishing enamel applied on it, and the film is then observed for uniformity and absorption. C-1. PROCEDURE C-1.1 Prepare a 300 � 150 � 0.900 mm mild steel panel and roughen it with emery paper. Wipe this with petroleum hydrocarbon solvent 145/205 ( low aromatic ) and allow to dry. Apply one coat of red oxide-zinc chromate primer ( see IS : 2074-1979* ) and allow to air-dry for 18 hours. Brush one coat of grey filler ( see IS : 110-1983 ) and allow to dry for 18 hours. Over this, make
*Specification for ready mixed paints, red oxide-zinc chrome, priming (first revision ). Specification for ready mixed paint, brushing, grey filler, for enamels, for use over primers ( second revision ). 3

4 applications of the material after an interval of 12 hours between the applications in order to give a total film thickness of 1.25 mm. Allow the final coat of the material to dry for 12 hours and wet rub with No. 180 to 220 abrasive paper. Wipe off and allow the coat to dry free from water. Brush on a coat of grey ready mixed filler ( conforming to IS : 110-1983* ) and allow to dry for 18 hours. Wet rub with No. 280 emery paper, wipe off and allow to dry free from water. Apply one coat of finishing enamel ( see IS : 2932-1974 ) and allow to dry for 12 hours. C-1.1.1 The material shall be deemed to have passed the test if the finish is uniform and shows equal absorption all over.
N O T E -- For the purpose of testing, all the materials shall be from the same source. *Specification for ready mixed paint, brushing, grey filler, for enamels, for use over primers ( second revision ). Specification for enamel, synthetic exerior ( a ) undercoating ; (b) finishing (first revision ).

APPENDIX D
( Clauses 0 2 and 3.8 )
DETERMINATION OF ADHESION AND COMPATIBILITY IN PAINT SYSTEM D-0. GENERAL D-0.1 This method is used to establish whether the adhesion of a coating to a substrate is at a generally adequate level This does not distinguish between higher levels of adhesion for which more sophisticated methods of measurement are required. D-1. APPARATUS D-1.1 Cutting Tool -- Sharp razor blade, scalpel, knife or other cutting devices. It is of particular importancc that the cutting edges be in good condition. D-1.2 Cutting Guide -- Steel or other hard metal straightedge to ensure straight cuts. D-1.3 Tape -- 25 mm wide, semitransparent pressure-sensitive tape with an adhesion strength of 44 6 � 2.8 g/mm width. The backing of the tape may consist of fibre-reinforced cellulose acetate, unplasticized ( poly vinyl chloride ) or polyester film D-1.4 Rubber Eraser -- on the end of a pencil D-1.5 Illumination -- A light source is helpful in determining whether the cuts have been made through the film to the substrate. D-2. TEST SPECIMENS D-2.1 A paint system shall be prepared as described below: a) Clean the surface either by shot or grit blast, by phosphating or by any appropriate chemical treatment; b) Brush immediately one coat of red oxidezinc chromate primer ( see IS . 20741979* ) and allow to dry for at least 18 hours. Rub down with waterproof emery paper No. 220. c) Brush one coat of grey filler ( see IS : 1101983 ) and allow to dry for at least 12 hours; d) Give 4 applications of the material, each application having a thickness of 0 250 to 0 40 mm of dry film at an interval of 12 hours between the applications. The overall film thickness of 4 applications shall be about 1 25 mm, sufficient to take care of undulations and dents noticed in the sheet metal work. Allow the final coat to dry for 24 hours; e) Wet rub the surface with No. 220 abrasive paper; *Specification for ready mixed paint, air drying, red oxide-zinc chrome, priming (first revision ). Specification for ready mixed paint, brushing, grey filler, for enamels for use over primers ( second revision ).
4

f) Brush one coat of grey filler (see IS : 1101983* ) and allow to dry for 18 hours; g) Wet rub the filler with No. 240 or 280 waterproof abrasive and brush one coat of undercoating of gulf red colour ( see IS : 2932-1974 ) and allow to dry for 12 hours. Rub down with waterproof emery paper No. 320; h) Brush one coat of gulf red synthetic enamel, finishing ( see IS : 2932-1974 ) and allow to dry for 18 hours before assessing the performance. D-3. PROCEDURE D-3.1 Select an area free of blemishes and minor surface imperfections. D-3.2 Make two cuts in the film each about 40 mm long that intersect near their middle with an angle between 30 and 45�. When making the incisions, use the straightedge and cut through the coating to substrate in one steady motion. D-3.3 Inspect the incisions for reflection of light from the metal substrate to establish that the coating film has been penetrated. If the substrate has not been reached make another cross in a different location. Do not attempt to deepen a previous cut as this may affect adhesion along the incision D-3.4 Remove two complete laps of the pressuresensitive tape from the roll and discard. Remove an additional length at a steady ( that is, not jerked ) rate and cut a piece about 75 mm long. D-3.5 Place the center of the tape at the intersection of the cuts with the tape running in the same direction as the smaller angles. Smooth the tape into place by finger in the area of the incisions and then rub firmly with the eraser on the end of a pencil. The colour under the transparent tape is a useful indication of when good contact has been made. D-3.6 Within 9 0 � 3 0 s of application, remove the tape by seizing the free end and pulling it off rapidly ( not jerked ) back upon itself at as close to an angle of 180� as possible. D-3.7 Repeat the test in two other locations on each test panel. D-3.8 The material shall be deemed to have passed the test if the stopper layer has a good adhesion over filler coat. Failure of adhesion between primer coat to metal surface, filler to primer coat or finish coat to fillers coat should not be the cause for rejection of stopper. Examination of failure should be confined to the stopper and filler interphase. *Specification for ready mixed paint, brushing, grey filler, for enamels for use over primers ( second revision ). Specification for enamel, synthetic, exterior (a) undercoating, (b) finishing (first revision ).
